title: Pedigree: Latency vs Cost — Narrative Bench Notes
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working narrative for product/ops teams to help communicate the tradeoffs between tail-latency targets and per-query cost under a small set of realistic conversational workloads. Audience: product PMs, SREs, performance engineers, and solutions engineering.

Summary (one-paragraph):
We ran three conversational workload personas against two model variants (baseline float32 large and quantized-8 hybrid) on a mid-range GPU fleet with our sessionized routing enabled. The objective: quantify how aggressive tail-SLOs (p95/p99) drive incremental cost when keeping median latency roughly constant via burst capacity and prewarm policies. Results show a steep marginal cost near p99 as we size for microburst headroom, while median-optimized configs keep cost low but suffer p99 regressions for spiky traffic.

Test matrix (short):
- Workloads:
  - Assist-long: longer contextual memory, average response tokens=420, 30% multi-turn sessions
  - Chat-snap: short quick responses, avg 24 tokens, high QPS burstiness (peak:median=22x)
  - Embed-mix: small text+metadata embeddings mixed with occasional 128-token responses
- Model variants:
  - Variant A: baseline float32 large (baseline-l40f)
  - Variant B: 8-bit hybrid quant + KV-compact path (quant-h8k)
- Infrastructure knobs:
  - Prewarm: off / conservative (1.2x steady) / aggressive (2.5x steady)
  - Burst pool: none / 10% reserved / 30% reserved
- Metrics collected: median latency (ms), p95, p99, cost per 1M tokens (USD), prewarm idle cost, throughput sustained

Narrative results (selected slices):
1) Chat-snap (burst-prone) — median-stable sizing vs p99 hedging
- Baseline-l40f + prewarm off: median=42ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms, cost/1M tokens=79 USD
- Baseline-l40f + conservative prewarm (1.2x): median=44ms, p95=120ms, p99=240ms, cost/1M tokens=104 USD (↑31%)
- Quant-h8k + conservative prewarm: median=46ms, p95=140ms, p99=320ms, cost/1M tokens=68 USD (↓34% vs baseline+prewarm)
- Key color: quantization reduces steady-state unit cost substantially but p99 still sensitive to burst pool sizing and KV cache warmup patterns.

2) Assist-long (session-heavy) — amortization benefits and KV cache hit dynamics
- Baseline-l40f + aggressive prewarm: median=310ms, p95=520ms, p99=830ms, cost/1M tokens=125 USD (prewarm wasted cycles ↑15% of spend)
- Quant-h8k + aggressive prewarm: median=330ms, p95=540ms, p99=790ms, cost/1M tokens=86 USD
- Observations: long sessions amortize prefix cost; quant variant gives clear cost advantage while preserving p99 if prewarm keeps KV warm. If prewarm is absent, p99 jumps more for quant path due to slower cold kv-inflate paths.

3) Embed-mix (hybrid traffic) — mixed requests change batching efficiency
- Baseline-l40f: median embedding latency=95ms, burst p95=240ms, cost/1M units=42 USD
- Quant-h8k (+small-batch-tuning): median=120ms (embeddings slightly slower), cost/1M units=28 USD
- Note: embeddings converted to smaller kernels in quant path; there is a throughput versus latency trade — quant improves dollars per unit but can regress tight median SLOs for embeddings unless batch window increased.

Text tables (simple):
Cost vs p99 trade (Chat-snap, 1M tokens baseline):
Mode                     | median(ms) | p99(ms) | cost/1M USD
-------------------------|------------|---------|-----------
baseline-off-prewarm     | 42         | 420     | 79
baseline-cons-prewarm    | 44         | 240     | 104
quant-cons-prewarm       | 46         | 320     | 68

Simple ASCII graph (cost increase vs p99 target for Chat-snap):
Targets: p95 -> p99 -> p999
Cost (normalized to median-optimized=1.0):
median-optimized : ██████████ 1.00
p95-hedged       : ████████████████ 1.30
p99-hedged       : ████████████████████████ 1.95
Explanation: ramping to protect p99 often requires >1.5x capacity or higher prewarm/burst reserve, causing near-doubling of unit spend in extreme cases.

Operational anecdotes (notes to share with SRE/Console):
- Cache priming strategy matters: sessions with repeated entity ops reached 65–78% KV hit after 6 requests; cold sessions often cause p99 spikes that dominate customer-facing error budgets.
- Routing fallbacks: automatically switching to quant variant under sustained load reduced immediate queueing but sometimes shifted latency to slightly higher median; perceived user impact depends on UI tolerance for extra 10–15% latency.
- Developer experience: exposing a "cost-sensitivity" slider in the Console (suggested UI copy below) helped PMs choose a policy that matches features to spend.

Suggested Console copy (short):
- "Latency SLO priority: Low / Balanced / High — determines prewarm, burst reserve, and model-variant fallback rules.
- Low: prioritizes cost-savings; may accept p99 > 400ms for bursty chat.
- Balanced: preserves p95 targets while limiting spend to <=1.4x baseline.
- High: minimizes p99; expect cost uplift and more reserved capacity"

Appendix: measurement caveats and follow-ups
- Our microbench harness uses synthetic Poisson arrivals and a measured burst multiplier to emulate product traffic; real-world burst shapes (heavy-tailed interarrival) could increase p99 sensitivity by another 10–25%.
- Next runs to schedule: include mixed-region routing (edge vs core) and GPU variant with more aggressive kernel fusion to see if p99 beta narrows without cost uplift.
- Action items:
  - (Amit) instrument a KV priming metric to show "seconds since last hit" per-tenant and expose heatmap in Console by Oct 5
  - (Sofia) prepare a short slide: "When to choose quant-h8k vs baseline" for Solutions Eng by Oct 10
  - (Maya) run a follow-up with heavy-tailed arrival model and include p999 sampling by Oct 12

Key takeaways for GTM/PM:
- Tradeoff archetype: median-friendly configs are low-cost but brittle for p99 under bursty chat; p99 protection costs escalate non-linearly. Quantization is a strong lever to reduce baseline unit cost but does not replace the need for headroom for microbursts and KV warmup.
- Console: recommend adding a clear SLO-to-cost estimator and a simple toggle that suggests model-variant + prewarm presets for common workload personas.

Raw artifact references and quick links (internal):

- dashboard prototype: internal/dashboard/obs/pedigree-snap

End of working narrative.
